## When to use this

Reach for `mapbox` whenever a task involves a Mapbox API: reading or writing styles, fetching tiles or static images, geocoding, querying tilesets, listing or inspecting access tokens. It is one binary, it needs no SDK, and every command answers on stdout in a shape a program can read.

Do not hand-write a `curl` against `api.mapbox.com` when a command exists — the command already knows the URL, the required parameters, the token and the error shape. `mapbox --schema <command>` prints all of that as JSON if you need to check before running.

## The one-minute version

```sh
mapbox auth whoami
mapbox styles list -u USERNAME
mapbox --schema styles list
```

The first says which token the next command will use and whose it is. The second runs a real request. The third describes a command without running it, which is the cheapest way to learn what one takes.

## Authentication

Every command that makes a request needs an access token. The CLI sends it as the `access_token` query parameter, so it is never one of the arguments listed in a reference page. It is resolved from these, highest first:

1. `--token`/`-t`, typed on the command line. Outranks everything, including `--use-login`.
2. `MAPBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN` in the environment. The legacy spelling `MapboxAccessToken` is read only by `mapbox tilesets-cli`, which forwards to a tool that accepts it. `--use-login` skips this step.
3. Credentials stored by `mapbox auth login`, refreshed automatically when stale. `--profile <NAME>` picks which set. **`auth login` is the one command here you cannot run.** It opens a browser and waits for a person to approve, so without a terminal it refuses with `interactive_required` rather than hanging. Use step 2.

If you are an agent, step 2 is the one that works: have `MAPBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN` set before running anything, and ask the person you are working for to provide one from account.mapbox.com if it is missing. Do not reach for `mapbox auth login` when a command reports no token — it cannot succeed without a human at a browser, and asking is faster than finding that out.

The account a URL asks for is separate from the token: pass `--username`/`-u`, set `MAPBOX_USERNAME`, or let a stored login supply it. A command whose URL has an account placeholder cannot run without one.

`--use-login` removes step 2, and only step 2 — a `--token` typed on the command line still wins. It is the flag to reach for when a token left in a shell profile is shadowing a login for a different account.

## The output contract

stdout carries the result and nothing else. Warnings, progress and errors go to stderr, so a pipe reads clean.

`--output`/`-o` takes `auto`, `text` or `json`, and defaults to `auto`: text at a terminal, JSON when stdout is a pipe or a file. So a script gets JSON without asking, and a person gets a table without asking. `MAPBOX_OUTPUT` sets the same thing for a session.

Three things are exempt, and each for a reason worth knowing:

- A binary response — a tile, a static image, a font glyph range — is written to stdout as bytes whatever `--output` says. Redirect it to a file.
- `--help` and `--version` are clap's own rendering, not a result.
- `mapbox tilesets-cli` forwards to another program, which has no equivalent option; `--output` written before it earns a warning on stderr and changes nothing.

`--id <ID>` picks one row out of a command that returns a list, in either mode.

## Errors

A failure exits non-zero and writes to stderr. Under `json` it is one object with a machine-readable `code`, a `message`, and `status` when the failure came from an HTTP response — so a caller can branch on the code rather than parsing prose. Under `text` it is the message, plus a tip where there is one to give.

Two codes are worth special-casing: `missing_subcommand` means the command line named a command group but no operation, and an HTTP `401` means the token is the problem — the message says which of the sources above supplied it.

## Dry runs

Every command that changes something takes `--dry-run`: it prints the request it would send, or the file it would change, and exits without doing it. Commands that only read do not have the flag, so its presence in a reference page's argument table is itself the answer to whether a command mutates anything.

Use it before any destructive command you have not run before. It costs nothing and it is the only way to see the resolved URL without spending the request.

## Describing a command as JSON

`mapbox --schema <command>` prints the full description of a command as JSON: every argument with its type, whether it is required, the values it accepts, where it lands in the request, and the method and URL template. It works at every level — `mapbox --schema` for the whole CLI, `mapbox --schema styles` for one service, `mapbox --schema styles list` for one command — and needs no token, because it makes no request.

Prefer it over `--help` when a program is choosing the arguments. The reference pages here shorten a description that will not fit a table cell; `--schema` has the whole of every one.

## `mapbox tilesets-cli` is a proxy

`mapbox tilesets-cli` forwards everything after the subcommand name, verbatim, to the separately-installed `tilesets` binary from the Python package `mapbox-tilesets`. Two consequences that catch everyone:

- A `mapbox` global written *after* `tilesets-cli` goes to the child, which has never heard of it. Write globals before the subcommand name: `mapbox --schema tilesets-cli`, not `mapbox tilesets-cli --schema`.
- `mapbox tilesets-cli --help` shows the child's help, not this CLI's.

Its token is resolved as above and passed in the child's environment rather than its argv, so it never appears in `ps`. A `--token` written after `tilesets-cli` is forwarded and wins, which is the documented way to use a different token for one call. `--use-login` is the mirror image: it makes a stored login outrank a token already exported in the shell — worth knowing, because the Tilesets API answers a wrong-account token with a bare `Not found` that points nowhere near the cause.

## Global options

Accepted by every command, in any position — except after `mapbox tilesets-cli`, per the section above.

| Option | Type | Values | Default | Environment | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--debug` | boolean |  |  | `MAPBOX_DEBUG` | Print request URLs to stderr for debugging. |
| `--id ID` | string |  |  |  | Show only the row with this id, from a command that returns a list. |
| `--output OUTPUT` `-o` | string | `auto`, `text`, `json` | `auto` |  | Output format. `auto` reads stdout: a terminal gets text, a pipe or redirect gets JSON [env: MAPBOX_OUTPUT=]. |
| `--profile PROFILE` | string |  |  |  | Named credential profile to use (default: "default"). |
| `--schema` | boolean |  |  |  | Describe the command as JSON instead of running it: its arguments, their types, and the request it would make. |
| `--timeout TIMEOUT` | string |  |  |  | Seconds to wait for one request, connection included. Defaults to 60, or 900 for an upload [env: MAPBOX_TIMEOUT=]. |
| `--token TOKEN` `-t` | string |  |  | `MAPBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Mapbox access token. |
| `--use-login` | boolean |  |  |  | Use credentials from `mapbox auth login`, ignoring any MAPBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN in the environment. |
| `--username USERNAME` `-u` | string |  |  | `MAPBOX_USERNAME` | Mapbox username. |
| `--yes` `-y` | boolean |  |  | `MAPBOX_YES` | Assume yes: never ask before a destructive command. |
